record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For the k-SUM problem, where k is fixed, the input consists of m integers and a goal sum S, and the task is to decide whether some k of the integers add up to S, prove any non-trivial lower bound in either the algebraic decision tree model or the algebraic computation tree model.

evidence.quote: Prove a non-trivial lower bound for the k-SUM problem in the algebraic decision tree model or in the algebraic computation tree model

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an integer k ≥ 2. In the k-SUM problem, the input consists of m integers a_1, ..., a_m together with a target integer S, and one must decide whether there exist indices 1 ≤ i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_k ≤ m such that a_{i_1} + a_{i_2} + ... + a_{i_k} = S.

Recall the following two models of computation on inputs viewed as points in R^m:

(a) Algebraic decision tree model. A computation is a rooted ternary tree whose internal nodes are labeled by polynomials p(x_1, ..., x_m) of bounded degree; the branch taken at a node depends on the sign (negative, zero, positive) of p evaluated on the input. Leaves are labeled "yes" or "no". The complexity is the depth (worst-case number of polynomial tests).

(b) Algebraic computation tree model. A computation tree in which each internal node either performs an arithmetic operation (+, −, ×, ÷, √) on previously computed values or the input variables, or branches on the sign of a previously computed value. The complexity is again the depth.

Problem: Establish any non-trivial (i.e., super-linear, or more generally super-(m log m)) lower bound on the depth required to solve the k-SUM problem in either the algebraic decision tree model or the algebraic computation tree model, for some fixed k ≥ 3.
artifact.category_tag: k-SUM lower bounds in algebraic decision trees
artifact.status_search_result: Only Ω(m log m) bounds (matching element distinctness, due to Ben-Or / Steele–Yao topological methods) are known for k-SUM in the general algebraic decision tree and algebraic computation tree models. Stronger lower bounds (e.g., Erickson's Ω(m^⌈k/2⌉)) are known only in restricted models such as k-linear decision trees. Recent results (Cardinale Tardos–type and Kane–Lovett–Moran near-linear linear decision trees) actually give surprisingly shallow trees, making non-trivial lower bounds in the algebraic model appear out of reach; the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Near-optimal Linear Decision Trees for k-SUM and Related Problems
status_evidence.snippet: There exist linear decision trees and algebraic computation trees of depth O(n^3 log^2 n) solving k-SUM.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bounds in the algebraic computation tree model are much smaller than any known lower bound, indicating that no strong lower bound is known.

status_evidence.title: On some fine-grained questions in algorithms and complexity
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open question whether k-SUM admits an algorithm of complexity O(n^c) with c < ceil(k/2).
status_evidence.claim: k-SUM complexity in algebraic models is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Lower bounds for algebraic decision trees
status_evidence.snippet: Topological method yields Ω(n log n) lower bounds for problems like element distinctness in algebraic decision trees.
status_evidence.claim: Standard topological techniques give at most Ω(m log m) bounds, not stronger ones for k-SUM.
